content:
Andrew Novak turned a six-shot overnight lead into his first individual PGA Tour title on Sunday at the Mexico Open at Vidanta Vallarta. The 31-year-old American closed with a 2-under 69 to finish at 25-under 259, a tournament record, winning by five shots over Steven Fisk and Kristoffer Ventura. Novak built the lead with rounds of 67, 61, 62 and 69, and after a bogey at the 10th cut his lead to three, he answered with three straight birdies on the back nine to put the tournament away.

It was Novak's first solo victory in his 140th PGA Tour start. His only previous tour win came in a team event, the 2025 Zurich Classic of New Orleans alongside Ben Griffin. The 259 breaks Tony Finau's 72-hole tournament record of 260 from 2023, and the five-shot margin is the largest in the event's history. Fisk and Ventura each closed with 63s, and Ventura's runner-up finish moved him from No. 108 to No. 76 in the FedExCup Fall standings, locking up his tour card for 2027. Griffin and Mackenzie Hughes tied for fourth at 265.

On the LPGA Tour, Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her Maybank Championship title in Malaysia, becoming the first player to win the event back to back. The Japanese star shot a final-round 68 to win by two shots over China's Yan Liu, holding the lead the rest of the way after two early birdies. It was Yamashita's fifth career LPGA Tour title, worth $450,000 and 500 Race to the CME Globe points, and it moved her to world No. 2. Liu's runner-up finish was her best on the LPGA Tour.

Elsewhere, Darren Fichardt of South Africa won the PGA Tour Champions' Simmons Bank Championship at 22 under, one shot ahead of Zach Johnson. The LPGA Tour's Asian swing concludes next week at the TOTO Japan Classic, where Nasa Hataoka will defend her 2025 title.

Sources: Associated Press via theScore; Golfmagic; Fairway to Green; Golf Today.

excerpt: Andrew Novak won the Mexico Open by five shots for his first individual PGA Tour title, and Miyu Yamashita became the first player to successfully defend the Maybank Championship on the LPGA Tour.
title: Golf Weekend: Novak Cruises to First Solo PGA Tour Title in Mexico, Yamashita Defends Maybank Championship
